subject: Demo recap + proposed POC scope and success criteria for Verdance Systems
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@verdance.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC scope and success criteria for Verdance Systems

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — appreciate the time. Below is a concise recap and a proposed POC (4-week) that we think will validate the two primary success criteria you called out: (1) accurate document extraction and routing for 10 common invoice templates, and (2) sub-second generation latency for aggregated order summaries under realistic traffic (burst to 15 req/s).

Proposed POC summary (high level):
- Duration: 4 weeks (two-week setup + two-week evaluation)
- Goals / success criteria:
  - Extraction accuracy >= 92% on the 10 invoice templates you provided (measured via labeled test set).
  - 95th percentile end-to-end response latency < 700ms for order-summary generation at 15 req/s burst test.
  - No more than 1 critical incident (availability) during the evaluation window.
- Scope: ingest sample invoice batch (up to 5k documents), set up a staging endpoint on Redwood Dedicated, run two scripted load tests, and run manual QA on 150 sampled records.
- Ownership: Redwood infra/setup — Karthik to provision dedicated capacity and run load tests; Customer data & test sets — Lydia / Samir to provide labeled samples and ACL access; CS lead — Jordan for onboarding and acceptance.
- Deliverables: POC runbook, config used for serving (batching/quantization profile), QA report with per-template accuracy, latency distribution chart, and recommended production config.
- Next steps (if we agree):
  1) Lydia to confirm scope and provide the labeled samples (or a secure S3 link) by Tue 5/9.
  2) Karthik will share an access checklist and security questionnaire that we need filled before provisioning in your VPC (if you choose Private) or to enable redwood-dedicated staging.
  3) Schedule 30-min kickoff during week of 5/13 — take turnkey times that work for your team.

Attachments: Verdance_POC_Scope_v1.pdf (summary + checklist), network-security-checklist.xlsx (short stub of required network rules).

If that aligns, I’ll drop a formal calendar invite and DocuSign for the POC amendment.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Park <lydia@verdance.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@edge-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC scope and success criteria for Verdance Systems

Thanks Rishi — that looks very close to what we discussed. Quick notes from our side:
- We can commit to the 4-week rhythm.
- I’ve looped in Samir (platform lead) to coordinate sample extraction and network requirements. Samir — we have an internal set of 3,200 invoices and a handful of edge cases (handwritten fields) we want included. Can you confirm a sanitized S3 link by 5/9?
- Two asks from security: we need your SOC2 evidence and the short network checklist completed (Samir will coordinate with his infra).

We’re very interested in the latency target; could you confirm whether those numbers assume a warmed KV cache and the specific instance type you plan to provision?

Lydia
VP Product | Verdance Systems

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@verdance.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 May 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC scope and success criteria for Verdance Systems

Lydia — thanks for the quick reply. A few clarifications from the infra side: 
- Latency/assumptions: the 95th <700ms target assumes a warmed runtime (KV cache active) and a dedicated pool using A10G-equivalent instances with continuous batching enabled. If you prefer a lower-cost variant we can provide an alternate profile and expected numbers.
- Data needs: sanitized S3 link or secure Share (we can accept a signed URL). Include a small labeled subset (150 records) for immediate QA; we’ll use that to validate extraction before running the full 3.2k sweep.
- Security artifacts: attaching the short network checklist here; I’ve also uploaded our SOC2 summary to the Drive link Rishi shared. Please note that for Private deployments we’ll need a short window to validate KMS integration (if using customer-managed keys).

Quick proposed timeline:
- Week 1 (5/15–5/19): Access & config, dataset intake, provisioning (Redwood + network checks).
- Week 2 (5/22–5/26): Model tuning + baseline runs on labeled subset.
- Week 3 (5/29–6/02): Full-run extraction + load tests.
- Week 4 (6/05–6/09): QA sampling, acceptance review, final report.

I’ll create the staging endpoint once we confirm the S3 link and the security checklist is acknowledged.

Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

(Attachment: network-security-checklist.xlsx)
